prompt: One continuous five-second high-speed camera move, bridging the provided first-person sprint start frame into the overhead race end frame. Riley keeps sprinting forward throughout. Opening 0–0.7s: first-person eye-level view racing along the boulevard at superhuman speed, peripheral scenery streaking backward and a natural alternating hand swing. From 0.7–2.2s the camera smoothly lifts up and falls a little behind Riley, tilting downward as her head, shoulders, gold dress and running legs enter beneath it, revealing that the POV belonged to her. This is one physically continuous rising crane/drone move through open air, not a cut, dissolve, morph, teleport or separate aerial scene. Keep the rail on screen-left and the glass frontage on screen-right; no sideways rotation or crossing the track. By 2.2s the camera is high overhead facing down and tracks forward. The train is moving briskly forward on the left rails, in the same up-screen direction. Riley is MUCH faster: she blasts up the separate right boulevard, races past the train's leading nose between 2.2–3.5s and increases the gap; her entire body and both boots clear the train nose. Finish in the supplied overhead end-frame composition with Riley fully ahead, still mid-sprint. Strong ground parallax and thin trailing cyan wake, high cadence athletic strides, no slow motion, walking, deceleration, hovering or freeze. Train stays aligned with its rails and continues forward; it never turns toward Riley or moves backward. Maintain the same continuous wet glass-and-chrome city, golden bollards, cyan accents, trees and pedestrian scale as the references. Consistent Riley: short brown bob, gold sleeveless short dress, black high boots, mostly natural skin with narrow chrome/cyan inlays; no wardrobe morph or duplicate Riley. Ambient fast wind, footfalls and train only; no speech, music, captions or logos.

model_guide.guide:
# Seedance family — bytedance-seedance-v1-pro, bytedance-seedance-v1.5-pro, bytedance-seedance-v2, bytedance-seedance-v2-fast, bytedance-seedance-v2.5, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-edit, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-extend, bytedance-seedance-v2-us, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-us, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-edit-us, bytedance-seedance-v2.5-extend-us

ByteDance's flagship video model. The first model supporting simultaneous quad-modal input (text, image, video, and audio). Strong motion realism, character consistency, and multi-shot storytelling.

## Inputs

- Text prompt
- Optional reference image. The model cites these as `@image1`, `@image2` — but do not type that yourself: place an `image_reference` part where the reference belongs and the backend renders the token there.
- Optional reference video
- Optional audio track (model choreographs video to sound, beat-matched)
- Parameters: resolution and duration vary by variant (see below)

## Variant notes

- **Seedance 2.0 / 2.0 Fast** — up to 4K (2.0) or 1080p (Fast); clips 4–15s.
- **Seedance 2.5** (`bytedance-seedance-v2.5`) — sharper realism; up to 1080p; clips up to 30s; much larger reference budget (upto 10 image, video, and audio refs). Prefer 2.5 over 2.0 unless the user names 2.0.
- **Seedance 2.5 Edit** (`bytedance-seedance-v2.5-edit`) — edit an existing clip by describing the change. Duration follows the source.
- **Seedance 2.5 Extend** (`bytedance-seedance-v2.5-extend`) — continue from the end of an existing clip. Prompt what happens next.
- **US-hosted variants** (`bytedance-seedance-v2-us`, `bytedance-seedance-v2.5-us`, `-edit-us`, `-extend-us`) — the same models served from US infrastructure, offered where the standard ids are not available; same resolutions as their counterparts, and 2.0 US takes no seed. Prompt them exactly like their counterparts.
- Fast and Pro / 2.5 share prompting style. Longer variants tolerate longer prompts.

## Prompt structure

```
[shot] + [subject] + [action] + [environment / lighting] + [style]
```

## Key strengths

- **Handles physical interactions** (pouring, splashing, hand-object contact) better than most models. Describe them concretely.
- **Good at weather and atmospheric effects.**
- **Audio-to-video** — upload an audio track and the model choreographs video to the sound with beat-matched cuts and lip sync.
- **Negative prompts work** — phrases like "no distortion, no stretching," "no grain, no shadows" are effective.
- **Seedream + Seedance pipeline** — generate reference images with Seedream, then use as visual references for maximum control.

## For image-to-video

- **Describe the motion, not the image.** "Camera slowly orbits around her" works far better than re-describing what she looks like.
- **Lock the character with consistency language** — add "maintain exact appearance from reference image" or "consistent character throughout, no deformation or drift."

## Rules

- **A wired audio reference needs `generate_audio` on.** With it off the render comes back silent and the track you connected is thrown away, so connecting audio turns it back on — never set it to false to keep a voiceover "clean".
- **Use one continuous action per clip.** Multi-beat narratives drift.
- **For start/end frame inputs**, write a prompt that bridges the two states ("from sealed package to fully revealed product"), not a static description.

## Example

> Wide tracking shot of a courier riding an electric scooter through a rainy Shanghai night market. Neon shopfronts reflect on wet pavement. Wisps of steam rise from food stalls as he weaves between pedestrians. Cinematic, slightly desaturated, shallow depth of field.

## What to avoid

- Re-describing the reference image in image-to-video prompts (wastes prompt budget).
- Abstract or heavily stylized prompts without specificity.

assistant_visual_review.method: 21 quarter-second overview samples; 13 finer camera-rise and 13 ending samples, native2s/4s/5s frames; full decode. Not continuous playback or independent listening.
observations: The shot begins in the exact approved sprint POV. The camera progressively lifts behind the head and shoulders around1.3–2.2s, becoming overhead by roughly3s, with no obvious cut in the samples.
Rail stays left, boulevard and glass facade stay right; wet paving, gold bollards, cyan accents and short brown hair/gold dress/black boots are recognizable.
Riley ends ahead of the train, including her trailing boot. This completes only very late, close to the final quarter-second.
Arms and legs change pose through the reveal; there is visible forward scenery movement and a cyan wake.
limitations: The train nose appears to drift backward relative to nearby planters in the late overhead section. Perspective and changing generated geometry complicate exact velocity, but forward train motion is not established; do not treat this as a clean race lock.
Her arm swing rises near her head and the dress appears strapless from behind, softening the exact approved wardrobe match.
Most of the five seconds are spent on the camera rise and approach; the clear lead has little screen time. User playback should judge speed and transition quality.
480p distant detail cannot establish precise face/cyberware continuity.
Native audio was decoded and measured only; no independent listening or speech-absence claim. Approved full ad and music/voice unchanged.
